items.rule: A radius joins the centre to a point on the circle. A diameter passes through the centre and has twice the radius length.
A chord is a line segment whose endpoints lie on the circle. A diameter is the longest chord.
items.example: \text{If }r=5\text{ cm, the diameter is a chord of length }10\text{ cm}

items.rule: The perpendicular drawn from the centre of a circle to a chord bisects the chord.
Equal chords of the same circle are equidistant from the centre.
items.example: AB=CD\text{ and }OM\perp AB,\ ON\perp CD\implies OM=ON

items.rule: The length of an arc is the same fraction of the circumference as its central angle is of 360 degrees.
The area of a sector is the same fraction of the circle's area as its central angle is of 360 degrees.
A tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius drawn to the point of contact.
Tangents drawn from the same external point to a circle have equal lengths.

concepts.title: 1. Circle Vocabulary
concepts.subtitle: Naming Parts of a Circle
concepts.summary: A circle is defined by its centre and constant radius. Important parts include radius, diameter, chord, arc, sector, segment, and tangent.

points.text: Centre: The fixed point from which every point on the circle is the same distance.
Radius: A segment from the centre to the circle.
Diameter: A chord through the centre, equal to $2r$.
Chord: A segment joining any two points on the circle.
Arc: A portion of the circumference between two points.
Sector: The region enclosed by two radii and the included arc.
Segment: The region enclosed by a chord and its corresponding arc.
Tangent: A line touching the circle at exactly one point.

concepts.trap: Do not confuse a diameter with an arbitrary chord. A diameter must pass through the centre.

concepts.title: 2. Chord Properties
concepts.subtitle: Centre-to-Chord Relationships
concepts.summary: A perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects that chord. Equal chords in the same circle lie at equal perpendicular distances from the centre.

points.text: Reverse Use: If the centre-to-chord perpendicular bisects a chord, it can be used to find half the chord immediately.
Equal Chords: Equal chords are equally distant from the centre.
Diameter as Chord: A diameter is the maximum-length chord because it passes through the centre.

concepts.trap: The theorem requires a perpendicular from the centre. An arbitrary segment from the centre to a chord does not necessarily bisect it.

concepts.title: 3. Arc Length & Sector Area
concepts.subtitle: Using the Central-Angle Fraction
concepts.summary: A sector with central angle θ represents θ/360 of the complete circle. The same fraction applies to circumference for arc length and to area for sector area.

points.text: Arc Length: Multiply the fraction $\frac{\theta}{360^\circ}$ by the circumference $2\pi r$.
Sector Area: Multiply the same angle fraction by the circle area $\pi r^2$.

concepts.trap: Do not use degrees as a fraction without dividing by 360. The central angle must represent the correct fraction of a full revolution.

concepts.title: 4. Tangent–Radius Relationship
concepts.subtitle: Perpendicularity and Equal Tangents
concepts.summary: At the point where a tangent touches a circle, the radius to the point of contact is perpendicular to the tangent. From a common external point, tangent segments to the same circle are equal.

points.text: Right Angle: Radius to the point of contact is perpendicular to the tangent.
Equal Tangents: Tangent segments drawn from the same external point have equal lengths.
Right-Triangle Link: The radius, tangent segment, and external-point distance often form a right triangle, allowing Pythagoras to be used.

concepts.trap: Equal tangent lengths apply only to tangents drawn from the same external point to the same circle.

worked_examples.title: Type 1: Using the Chord-Bisector Property
worked_examples.problem: A chord AB of a circle is 16 cm long. The perpendicular from the centre O meets AB at M. Find AM and MB.

steps.reason: The perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects the chord.
M divides the chord into two equal parts.
Each half is half the total chord length.

worked_examples.conclusion: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, so AM=MB=8 cm.

worked_examples.title: Type 2: Arc Length and Sector Area
worked_examples.problem: A sector has radius 6 cm and central angle 60°. Find its arc length and area.

steps.statement: Find the fraction of the full circle:
steps.reason: The sector subtends one-sixth of a complete revolution.
Arc length is the same fraction of circumference.
Sector area is the same fraction of the full circle area.

worked_examples.conclusion: The arc length is 2π cm and the sector area is 6π cm².

worked_examples.title: Type 3: Equal Tangents from an External Point

worked_examples.conclusion: The second tangent is also 9 cm long.
